posts.title: Death toll passes 359 as Nepal watches for a second flood
body: Nepal Police said 359 bodies have been recovered as of Thursday evening, spokesperson Abi Narayan Kafle told the Kathmandu Post. The flood hit Timure in Rasuwa on Wednesday morning and ran down the Bhote Koshi into the Trishuli and the Narayani. Chitwan has the most dead, 132, followed by Nawalparasi East with 82 and Dhading with 33, the Kathmandu Post reports.

The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority says 910 people remain out of contact. Of those, 570 are tourists. Nepal's tourism board says 517 of the missing are foreign nationals from 33 countries, with India's 178 the highest, followed by 65 Americans and 53 Ukrainians.
Out of contact does not mean dead. Phone lines, power and internet are down across the valley and are coming back slowly.

A second flood is still possible. Nepal's Department of Hydrology and Meteorology says a lake has formed on the Lhende river, about 18 kilometres upstream of the Rasuwagadhi border crossing, where the original collapse happened. The lake covers around 0.11 square kilometres and is still rising, the department says. China passed the warning on through Nepal's foreign ministry.

USGS first read the shaking as an earthquake. It later found no earthquake took place. The signal came from an ice and rock avalanche that fell into the Lhende Khola on the Tibet side, dammed the river, then broke.

Nepal's Army says more than 5,000 army and police personnel are working the flood zone, from Nuwakot to Chitwan. Prime Minister Balendra Shah travelled to Bidur in Nuwakot on Thursday to see the damage.
In India, the NDRF and the Sashastra Seema Bal have rescue teams on standby in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh. The NDRF says the Gandak, which the Narayani becomes downstream, could see higher water levels.
Keep off the banks of the Bhote Koshi, the Trishuli and the Narayani until officials say it is clear.

posts.title: Damage put at Rs 200 billion, hydropower losses still being counted
body: Physical Infrastructure Minister Sunil Lamsal said damage to roads and bridges is around Rs 200 billion. He called it preliminary information.

That figure does not include energy infrastructure. Energy Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha has ordered an immediate assessment of hydropower damage. In Rasuwa, 8 projects have been hit, 5 of them operational with a combined 236 megawatts, and 3 still under construction with a combined 342 megawatts. Nuwakot has lost access to 6 more projects, 4 operational at 123 megawatts and 2 under construction at 53 megawatts.
Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading and Chitwan are still being surveyed for road and building damage, so the Rs 200 billion figure is expected to rise.

The government has released Rs 1 billion to the disaster relief fund, plus Rs 10 million each to Rasuwa and Nuwakot and Rs 5 million to Dhading. The World Bank has separately offered up to Rs 25 billion in emergency assistance, its Nepal country director told the finance ministry. That is aid, not a damage estimate.
Insurers say claims will take weeks to settle because most of the damaged sites cannot be reached by road.
